input_consistency.note: All three implementations use identical input parameters. Ground motion normalized to 0.40g PGA. ABAQUS uses CLOAD (concentrated force) for ground motion application; MATLAB uses effective force; OpenSeesPy uses UniformExcitation.

hysteresis.note: Hysteresis data available for all three software. MATLAB and OpenSeesPy show similar bilinear kinematic hardening loops. ABAQUS shows larger hysteresis area due to larger displacement response.

yielding_sequence.matlab: yield_flags.txt available - isolation layer yields first, superstructure stories yield progressively
yielding_sequence.openseespy: material-level yielding tracked via Steel01 state
yielding_sequence.abaqus: connector plasticity tracked via CTF field output

early_time_match.matlab_abaqus_t0_to_t1s: PASS - near-identical response for first ~1 second

abaqus_diagnosis.early_linear_match: PASS - first 1.0s of ABAQUS response matches MATLAB reference within 1%
abaqus_diagnosis.nonlinear_divergence: ABAQUS diverges after yielding onset. Likely causes: (a) Chaboche kinematic hardening model in ABAQUS connectors differs from MATLAB bilinear return mapping, (b) CONN3D2 element formulation produces different tangent stiffness during plastic flow, (c) combined isotropic+kinematic hardening in default connector hardening may activate unintended isotropic component.
abaqus_diagnosis.status: PARTIAL - linear elastic regime verified, nonlinear regime divergent

overall_assessment.matlab_vs_openseespy: PASS - peak displacement within 12.3%, acceleration within 2.0%, base shear within 2.0%. These differences are acceptable for nonlinear seismic analysis of isolated structures.
overall_assessment.matlab_vs_abaqus: PARTIAL - early-time linear response matches perfectly. Nonlinear response diverges significantly (displacement 3x, base shear 3.7x). ABAQUS connector hardening implementation differs from the explicit return-mapping algorithm used in MATLAB.
overall_assessment.recommendation: MATLAB and OpenSeesPy results are mutually consistent and cross-validated. ABAQUS requires further investigation of connector hardening model parameters to match the bilinear kinematic hardening return mapping used in MATLAB.
